issues.legal_issue: A registered sale deed transfers title when its terms show an absolute sale and do not make transfer conditional on payment or performance of a further obligation.
material_facts: The sellers executed and registered a deed stating that they absolutely sold the property for the specified consideration and put the purchasers in possession.
The deed provided for part of the consideration to be applied to the mortgage debt, part to be set off against an amount owed to the purchasers, and the remainder to be paid to the sellers.
The High Court found that the purchasers paid the disputed cash amount, and the purchasers deposited the remaining balance in court.
The deed contained no term making transfer of title conditional on full payment, payment of the mortgage debt, or delivery of the registration receipt.
The sellers retained the registration receipt, but the court treated this as resulting from subsequent events rather than evidence of a condition on transfer.
issues.conclusion: Title passed to the purchasers upon execution and registration of the sale deed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 8 and 54 of the Transfer of Property Act, ownership and transferable interests pass on a registered sale unless a different intention is expressed or necessarily implied. The party asserting that title did not pass must establish that intention from the deed or, if it is ambiguous, from attending circumstances, subject to Section 92 of the Evidence Act. Panchoo Sahu v. Janki Mandar illustrates a deed expressly conditioning passage of title on payment; Hara Bewa v. Banchanidhi Barik illustrates resort to surrounding circumstances where the deed is ambiguous. The court also found the other cited decisions consistent with this approach.

rule.if: sale_title_dispute and registered_sale_deed and deed_expresses_absolute_sale and possession_delivered and no_title_condition_in_deed

predicates.sale_title_dispute: A proceeding concerns whether a purchaser acquired title to property under a sale.
predicates.registered_sale_deed: The seller executed and registered a deed of sale for the property.
predicates.deed_expresses_absolute_sale: The deed describes the transfer as an absolute sale rather than a conditional transfer.
predicates.possession_delivered: The seller put the purchaser in possession of the property.
predicates.no_title_condition_in_deed: The deed does not state that title will pass only after payment or performance of a further obligation.

issues.definition: When a proceeding concerns title under a registered sale deed that expresses an absolute sale, transfers possession, and contains no condition delaying title, title passes on registration.

issues.legal_issue: A purchaser's failure to deposit mortgage money in court before bringing a redemption claim does not, by itself, defeat the claim when the property was sold subject to the mortgage.
material_facts: The sale deed made provision for the purchasers to pay the mortgage debt, and the property was transferred subject to the mortgage.
The purchasers did not deposit the mortgage money in court with their plaint but later deposited it under the trial court's decree and redeemed the mortgage.
The High Court treated the absence of a deposit with the plaint as fatal to the purchasers' case.
issues.conclusion: The failure to deposit the mortgage money in court before suit was not fatal; the purchasers redeemed the mortgage by depositing the amount under the decree.
issues.legal_principle: The court agreed with Shiva Narayan Sah v. Baidya Nath Prasad Tiwary that depositing the mortgage amount in court is one of three available modes before filing a redemption suit, and a mortgagor may choose another mode. Where the sale is subject to a mortgage, the purchaser's obligation to discharge the mortgage is not unpaid sale consideration whose non-payment prevents title from passing.

rule.if: mortgage_redemption_dispute and property_sold_subject_to_mortgage and buyer_did_not_deposit_mortgage_money_before_suit and buyer_later_redeemed_mortgage

predicates.mortgage_redemption_dispute: A proceeding concerns a purchaser's claim to redeem a mortgage affecting purchased property.
predicates.property_sold_subject_to_mortgage: The seller transferred the property while it remained subject to a mortgage.
predicates.buyer_did_not_deposit_mortgage_money_bef: The purchaser did not deposit the mortgage money in court before bringing the claim.
predicates.buyer_later_redeemed_mortgage: The purchaser later paid or deposited the mortgage amount and redeemed the mortgage.

issues.definition: When a redemption dispute concerns property sold subject to a mortgage, the purchaser's failure to deposit the mortgage money before suit does not defeat the claim if the purchaser later redeems the mortgage.

issues.legal_issue: A seller cannot unilaterally cancel a completed sale after title has passed, and a subsequent sale by that seller is ineffective against the first purchaser.
material_facts: The court found that title passed to the first purchasers under the registered sale deed.
The sellers later executed a document purporting to cancel that deed and then executed a second sale deed in favour of other purchasers.
The first purchasers challenged both later documents as invalid and not binding on them.
issues.conclusion: The sellers could not unilaterally cancel the first sale, and the later cancellation and sale did not defeat the first purchasers' title.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 8 and 54 of the Transfer of Property Act, a registered sale transfers ownership unless a different intention is expressed or necessarily implied. Once the deed transferred title without a condition delaying its passage, the sellers could not undo that transfer by executing a unilateral cancellation document; they could not convey to subsequent purchasers title that had already passed.

rule.if: sale_title_dispute and title_already_passed_to_first_buyer and seller_later_executes_unilateral_cancellation and seller_later_resells_property

predicates.sale_title_dispute: A proceeding concerns competing claims to property under successive sale documents.
predicates.title_already_passed_to_first_buyer: The first buyer acquired title under the earlier sale.
predicates.seller_later_executes_unilateral_cancell: The seller later executes a cancellation document without the first buyer's agreement.
predicates.seller_later_resells_property: The seller later executes another sale of the same property to a different buyer.

issues.definition: When title has passed to the first buyer and the seller later unilaterally cancels the sale and resells the property, those later acts are ineffective against the first buyer.
